# spotlight_egress (Resource)

An egress that the runners of push pools send their traffic through. A `spotlight_runner_pool` names it in `provision.egress`. For each run, the egress adds the secrets of the run to the requests that go to their bound hosts. A bound host is a host that a secret of the run is bound to. The egress calls Spotlight with its token. Spotlight does not delete an egress while a pool names it. Terraform can delete the egress before it updates the pools, so first remove `provision.egress` from the pools and apply, then remove the egress. Writing egresses needs a token granted the `runners` scope. Import it as `<workspace id>/<key>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
locals {
  shared = {
    key           = "shared"
    token_version = 1
  }
}

resource "random_password" "egress" {
  length  = 48
  special = false

  keepers = local.shared
}

resource "spotlight_egress" "shared" {
  workspace_id  = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  key           = local.shared.key
  url           = "https://egress.example.com"
  token         = random_password.egress.result
  token_version = local.shared.token_version
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Names the egress, as in `shared`. It is fixed for the egress's life, so changing it replaces the egress.
- `url` (String) Where the runners of a pool that names the egress send their traffic, as in `https://egress.example.com`. It has no credentials, no query and no fragment. An http URL gets a warning: the runners send their proxy credential to it, and a production deployment does not provision runners that use it.
- `workspace_id` (String) The workspace the egress belongs to. Changing it replaces the egress.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `token` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The token the egress calls Spotlight with: 32 to 255 URL-safe characters, as a generated password would be. Spotlight keeps only its hash. Left out, Spotlight issues one when it creates the egress, which Terraform does not keep; a change to `token_version` must come with a token. Each token is single-use. Spotlight does not accept the token of another egress. A token that you rotated away, or that a deleted or replaced egress used, was used once, so no egress accepts it again, the same egress included. Thus, to rotate or replace an egress, you always need a new token. It is sent to Spotlight and never stored in the plan or the state, so it needs Terraform 1.11 or later; change `token_version` to send it again.
- `token_version` (Number) Any number; change it whenever `token` changes, so Terraform sends the new value.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Names the resource within its workspace, as in `shared`.
- `id` (String) Issued by Spotlight when the egress is created, and never changed.
- `version` (Number) Rises with every change to the egress; each write sends it back so a change made since is not overwritten.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_egress.shared
  identity = {
    id = "3c9a7e15-2b64-4d8f-a1e0-6f4b2d8c7a19"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The id Spotlight issued the egress when it was created.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_egress.shared
  id = "5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/shared"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an egress with the id of its workspace and its key.
terraform import spotlight_egress.shared 5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/shared
```
